$comment: THE cinematography vocabulary. schema.py, style.py, dojo_study.py, dojo_measure.py (Python, via pipeline/vocab/vocab.py) and vocabulary.ts, CullGrid.tsx (TypeScript, via lib/vocab/cinematography.ts) derive from this file; pipeline/check-vocab.mjs enforces it. Bump `version` whenever an enum, weight or field set changes; every enum value must be covered by an `evidence` entry (the measured reason it exists). For an ordinal field the enum order IS the scale.

craft.description: Per-frame camera, lens, light and composition annotation (schema.py).

style.description: Art-style observables, read per source set or per image (style.py, foundry extractor).

face_state.description: The performer's face: closed enums for the state-freeze probe (dojo_measure.py).

shot_size.description: How much of the main subject the frame holds.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

camera_angle.description: Where the camera sits relative to the subject's eyeline.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

angle_evidence.description: The visual cue that proves the angle, in under 15 words (converging verticals, visible ceiling, ground plane height).

lens_impression.description: The lens register the image reads as -- from perspective stretch and edge behaviour, NOT a guessed focal length. Answer 'indeterminate' unless the frame actually shows a cue: visible edge distortion, stretched foreground, or compressed background separation. A tight shot with no visible depth cues is indeterminate, and saying so is correct.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

Measured 2026-08-25 on a 36-frame animation corpus the field answered 'wide-angle' 34 times out of 36, including on every extreme close-up where nothing reveals a lens register; a field that returns the same value regardless of input carries no information, so the model needs a legitimate way to decline.

lens_evidence.description: The cue behind the lens call, under 15 words (edge distortion, background compression, foreground exaggeration). If indeterminate, say what is missing.

depth_of_field.description: How much of the depth is in focus.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

subject_scale.description: How large the main subject sits in frame, as a fraction of height, e.g. 'about one third'.

composition.description: How the subject is placed in the rectangle.

evidence.finding: Added for the replication lane: layers and light alone do not pin a frame down, and a replica that gets light and lens right but composition wrong has not understood the shot.

exposure.description: Overall brightness of the frame. This is the BRIGHTNESS question -- answer it here, not in lighting_key.

evidence.finding: Added so lighting_key can stop being a brightness detector: in the 2026-08-25 run 22 of 36 frames came back both high-key and high-contrast while a luma check showed the field tracking mean brightness almost perfectly (143 vs 68).

true_black_share.description: How much of the frame is true black holding no detail at all. Look at the darkest regions and estimate their area: none, a small portion, or a large portion.

evidence.finding: An observable, not a term of art: if the model cannot reason from shadow depth to the high-key/low-key label, the label is derived in code from how much of the frame is true black.

lighting_key.description: The key-to-fill RATIO, which is about shadow depth and NOT about brightness. high-key = shadows filled in, few dark areas, gentle falloff. low-key = shadows left unfilled, much of the frame falling to black. A bright frame with deep black shadows is LOW-key; a dim frame lit evenly with no true blacks is HIGH-key. Judge the darkest areas, not the brightest.

evidence.finding: Redefined as the key-to-fill ratio (shadow depth), not brightness; exposure now carries the brightness answer.

lighting_direction.description: Dominant direction the key light comes from.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.
Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

contrast.description: Distance between the brightest and darkest areas that carry detail.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.

light_sources.description: Light sources visible or clearly implied IN the frame (practical lamps, fire, screens, sun, emissive props).

palette.description: The colour scheme in under 12 words.

foreground.description: What occupies the foreground layer, under 20 words. 'empty' if nothing.

midground.description: What occupies the midground layer -- usually the subject -- under 20 words.

background.description: What occupies the background layer, under 20 words.

subjects.description: The people or creatures in frame and what each is doing.

surrounding_objects.description: Notable set objects and props that establish the place.

texture.description: Surface character of the image itself.

evidence.finding: Per-frame texture later collapsed to glossy-cg on 86-93% of frames for four of six sources, which is why style moved to the per-source pass (style group).

genre_register.description: The genre contract the frame's light, camera and palette belong to.

evidence.finding: Lifted verbatim from the ai-registry media-generation / visual-generation / cinematic-language subject, so an annotation that validates is already registry-shaped.
Lets a labeller flag a frame it could not read instead of hiding the doubt in prose.

render_mode.description: How the images are made, judged from surfaces and edges rather than subject matter.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

passDescriptions.style_image: How the image is made, judged from surfaces and edges rather than subject matter.

detail_density.description: How much incidental detail fills the frame -- set dressing, wear, background business.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

passDescriptions.style_image: How much incidental detail fills the frame — set dressing, wear, background business.

surface_realism.description: How convincingly materials behave: skin, metal, cloth, stone.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

atmospherics.description: Particulate and haze in the air across these frames.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

passDescriptions.style_image: Haze, fog and volumetric light in the air — the air itself.

palette_strategy.description: How colour is organised across the set.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

passDescriptions.style_image: How colour is organised across the frame.

black_handling.description: What happens in the darkest areas.

evidence.finding: Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.
Observable vocabulary shared by pipeline/vlm-probe/style.py and the foundry extractor, so an extracted style and a read-back one compare field by field.

motion_treatment.description: How movement is rendered where visible.

evidence.finding: style.py's own ninth observable: how movement is rendered where visible.

consistency_across_frames.description: Whether these frames look like one production. A source whose own style varies is a finding.

evidence.finding: A source whose own style varies is a finding, so the per-source pass records whether the frames look like one production.

signature.description: What makes this look distinctive, under 25 words. Name properties, not titles or franchises.

imitable_recipe.description: How you would instruct an image generator to reproduce this look, under 40 words. Concrete visual instructions only -- no proper nouns, no studio or franchise names.

medium.description: What the image physically IS: a photograph; a 3D render (modelled forms, consistent specular, CG hair/cloth); a 2D digital painting (brushed or airbrushed shading on flat forms, painted hair as shapes); traditional paint on a real surface; a line drawing (pencil, ink); or mixed media.

evidence.finding: Added 2026-08-27 after the first live run: a smooth 2D painting and a stylised 3D render are both stylised-realistic / plausible / soft in the original seven, so a replica that slipped from painting to render scored 0.875 while the eye said the medium was wrong.

particle_fx.description: Floating debris IN the air, distinct from haze: none; subtle dust motes; heavy environmental debris (embers, snow, sparks, ash); or glowing energy effects. A clean studio render and an ember-swept action frame differ HERE.

evidence.finding: Fidelity axis added 2026-08-27: airborne debris distinct from haze, so a clean studio render and an ember-swept action frame differ here.

finish.description: Micro-texture of surfaces: pristine and smooth; weathered with dirt, scratches and grit; or visibly brush-painted.

evidence.finding: Fidelity axis added 2026-08-27 after the first run's cull merged clean studio renders with gritty ember-swept key art; nothing in the vocabulary could see grit.

focus.description: Lens behaviour: sharp front to back; a shallow photographic depth of field with blurred bokeh background; or dominated by motion blur.

evidence.finding: Fidelity axis added 2026-08-27: true shallow-focus photography merged with deep-focus renders because nothing could see lens behaviour.

mouth.description: What the subject's mouth is doing.

evidence.finding: dojo_measure's performer channel: neither the craft schema nor the style read has a field for the face, so a state freeze walked through both. Closed enums so the probe's outcome is a count of landings.
